name: Handsel Monday

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Handsel Monday, also called Di-luain an t-sainnseil, is a Scottish festival. It falls on the first Monday after Hogmanay, the Scottish New Year's Day. The day was given to divination, or foretelling through games of chance and trial. On the Isle of Skye this Monday began a sequence of twelve days. The weather of each day was read as soothsaying for the twelve coming months. The holiday's name comes from the Scottish sainnseal. This was the gift offered to every visitor on that day.
objective: Document Handsel Monday, the Scottish festival of divination after the New Year.
